artworks.title: Perseus Turning Phineus and His Followers to Stone
artworks.description: The wedding feast freezes mid-riot: Perseus raises Medusa's head while Phineus and his armed followers stiffen into stone — Ovid's climax for the Ethiopian rival who claimed Andromeda first. The canvas tradition makes Phineus the antagonist of the Gorgon-slayer's marriage, not the Thracian seer of the Argonauts.

artworks.title: Phineus Attacking Perseus at the Wedding
artworks.description: This LACMA print stages Phineus' assault on the bridal feast — Cepheus' brother (or betrothed rival) interrupting Perseus and Andromeda before the Gorgon's head ends the fight. It is the visual type that separates Ethiopian Phineus from the Harpy-plagued king of Salmydessus.

artworks.title: Phineus Interrupts the Wedding of Perseus and Andromeda
artworks.description: A Dutch Metamorphoses plate titles the interruption: Phineus storms the banquet of Perseus and Andromeda. Print series carried Ovid's Ethiopian wedding war into countless Northern editions.

artworks.title: Phineus Interrupting the Wedding of Perseus and Andromeda
artworks.description: Van Wijnen's Baroque oil packs the feast with chaos as Phineus leads the attack — the rejected suitor whose petrifaction closes Andromeda's bridal night in Ovid's telling.
